title: Learning SYK Hamiltonians
authors: Anurag Anshu, Srinivasan Arunachalam, Sitan Chen, Yeongwoo Hwang
abstract: We study the problem of learning the dense Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev (SYK) Hamiltonian from copies of its Gibbs state. Existing algorithms for Hamiltonian learning typically rely on geometric locality or bounded interaction degree and therefore do not apply to SYK, where each quartic interaction overlaps with $Θ(n^3)$ others. We show that this obstruction can be overcome by exploiting the random mean-field structure of the model. At any constant temperature, we prove that with high probability over the SYK couplings, the entire Hamiltonian can be learned to inverse-polynomial accuracy using polynomially many samples. Furthermore, when the inverse temperature is restricted to be a sufficiently small constant, we construct a quasipolynomial-time learning algorithm which is qualitatively different from the sample-efficient algorithm.
summary: This paper tackles the challenging problem of reconstructing the complex, dense Hamiltonian of the SYK model solely from measurements of its thermal Gibbs state. By exploiting the model's random mean-field nature, the authors derive sample complexity bounds showing that the Hamiltonian can be learned efficiently, even when traditional locality assumptions fail.
main_problem: The core problem is learning the dense Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) Hamiltonian from measurements of the system's Gibbs state.
main_result: The authors prove that the SYK Hamiltonian can be learned to high accuracy using a sample complexity that is polynomial in system size, overcoming limitations faced by algorithms designed for local interactions.
method: The approach exploits the random mean-field structure of the SYK model, utilizing techniques from statistical inference (like maximum entropy methods) adapted for quantum expectation values.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the SYK model, a strongly interacting quantum many-body system characterized by all-to-all quartic interactions, leading to a dense Hamiltonian structure.
key_observables: The Gibbs state ($\gamma_{\vec{g}}$), quartic expectation values ($\mu_{ eta,I}$), and the log-partition function ($\Phi(\vec{g})$) are central observables.
important_parameters: The inverse temperature ($ eta$), the interaction order ($q$), and the desired accuracy ($\epsilon$) are key parameters governing the learning bounds.
main_assumptions: The success of the sample-efficient learning relies fundamentally on the random mean-field structure of the SYK couplings.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem of Hamiltonian learning for dense systems, presents the sample-efficient recovery algorithm for fixed $ eta$, and discusses a separate, time-efficient algorithm for small constant $ eta$.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the challenge of characterizing complex, highly entangled quantum systems (like those modeled by SYK) using limited experimental measurements, which is a major goal in quantum simulation and quantum information.
